editorial:
Set in Italy during 1916, this film follows two everyday guys, Oreste Jacovacci and Giovanni Busacca, who get drafted into World War I and spend most of their time trying to dodge duty. Instead of a serious war story, you get a funny, warm look at two regular people caught in something way bigger than them. The humor comes from their schemes, arguments, and the absurd situations they land in, which makes the whole thing feel surprisingly human and relatable. It is the kind of movie that makes you laugh while quietly reminding you how scary and unfair war really is.

The acting is the real highlight here, with both leads bringing charm and heart to every scene. The pacing moves along nicely, mixing laughs with heavier moments without feeling jarring. On the downside, some jokes may feel dated, and the tone shifts can catch you off guard. Still, if you enjoy classic European cinema or war stories with a sense of humor, this one is worth your time.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Oreste and Giovanni are captured by Austrian forces after a chaotic battle. They are given a chance to save themselves by revealing Italian troop positions, but they refuse and are executed. The twist is that these two men, who spent the whole movie trying to avoid duty and look out for themselves, end up dying as quiet heroes. Their sacrifice is not celebrated or remembered, which makes the ending both sad and powerful.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic war comedies with heart.
